proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, §4, the paragraph defining sets of locally finite perimeter and (4.1), chapter-03.txt lines 555-573 (printed p. 80): “E has locally finite perimeter in U if χ_E is in BV_loc(U) (See §2 of Ch. 2.) Thus E has locally finite perimeter in U if there is a Radon measure μ_E (= |Dχ_E| in the notation of §2 of Ch. 2) on U and a μ_E-measurable ν with |ν| = 1 μ_E-a.e. in U such that (4.1) ∫_{E∩U} div g dL^{n+1} = −∫_U g·ν dμ_E”. The printed justification is Simon Ch. 2, §2, (2.1)-(2.4) (chapter-02.txt lines 477-530, printed pp. 48-49): the functional ∫ u div g extends to compactly supported continuous fields and the Riesz representation theorem (Ch. 1, 4.14) gives μ, ν; “|Du| … is uniquely characterized by (2.4)”. We fill in the extension step, the converse, and the uniqueness (which the book asserts through the phrase “the” measure |Dχ_E|). Sign: the contract (and the printed (4.1)) has the minus sign, so ν is the inward normal; Ch. 2 (2.2) is printed without it, which only changes ν to −ν.

Notation. N := n + 1, ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), L^N = volume, div g = trace of Dg (SimonGMT euclideanDivergence). A Gauss-Green pair (μ, ν) for (U, E) (IsGaussGreenPair) means: μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ν μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e.; and (GG) ∫_{E∩U} div g dL^N = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ U. HasLocallyFinitePerimeter U E is SimonGMT IsLocallyBV U χ_E: U open, χ_E locally integrable on U, and for every open W with W̄ compact ⊆ U there is c(W) ≥ 0 with ∫_W χ_E div g ≤ c(W)·sup|g| for all C¹ g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ^N) with tsupport g ⊆ W.

Statement. For U open and E Lebesgue-null-measurable: (i) HasLocallyFinitePerimeter U E ⟺ ∃ μ ν, IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν; (ii) any two pairs (μ, ν), (μ', ν') satisfy μ = μ' and ν = ν' μ-a.e.

Proof.

1. Two remarks. (R1) If g is C¹ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U then div g = 0 off tsupport g (SimonGMT support_euclideanDivergence_subset), so ∫_{E∩U} div g = ∫_{E∩W} div g = ∫_W χ_E div g. (R2) For g as in (GG), x ↦ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ is bounded and vanishes off the compact tsupport g ⊆ U, where μ is finite; so it is μ-integrable and |∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ| ≤ sup|g|·μ(tsupport g).

2. “⇐”. Let (μ, ν) be a pair. U is open by hypothesis. χ_E is measurable for the completed Lebesgue measure (E is null-measurable) and bounded, hence locally integrable on U. Let W be open with W̄ compact ⊆ U and put c(W) := μ(W̄) (finite, ≥ 0). For C¹ g ∈ C_c with tsupport g ⊆ W: by (R1), (GG), |ν| = 1 a.e. and (R2), ∫_W χ_E div g = ∫_{E∩U} div g = −∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≤ ∫_{tsupport g}|g| dμ ≤ sup|g|·μ(W̄). Since compactlySupportedSupNorm g = sup_x |g(x)|, IsLocallyBV U χ_E holds.

3. “⇒”, Step 1: the functional on C¹ fields (Simon Ch. 2, (2.1), lines 482-493). Assume IsLocallyBV U χ_E. For C¹ g with compact support in U set Λ(g) := ∫_{E∩U} div g. If tsupport g ⊆ W (W open, W̄ compact ⊆ U), then by (R1) Λ(g) = ∫_W χ_E div g ≤ c(W) sup|g|, and applying this to −g, |Λ(g)| ≤ c(W) sup|g|.

4. “⇒”, Step 2: extension to continuous fields (Simon lines 485-490: “the functional ∫ u div g extends uniquely to give a linear functional on K(U, ℝⁿ) … bounded on K_W(U, ℝⁿ) for every W ⊂⊂ U”). Let g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be continuous with compact support K ⊆ U. Choose an open W with K ⊆ W, W̄ compact ⊆ U, and σ₀ < dist(K, ℝ^N ∖ W). The mollifications g_σ := φ_σ * g (σ < σ₀, φ_σ a standard mollifier) are C^∞ with support in the σ-neighbourhood of K ⊆ W and g_σ → g uniformly as σ → 0. By Step 3, |Λ(g_σ) − Λ(g_τ)| ≤ c(W) sup|g_σ − g_τ| → 0, so Λ̃(g) := lim_{σ→0} Λ(g_σ) exists. The limit does not depend on choices: for any sequence of C¹ fields hᵢ → g uniformly with supports in a fixed compact subset of U, |Λ(hᵢ) − Λ(g_σ)| ≤ c(W') sup|hᵢ − g_σ| for a W' ⊂⊂ U containing all supports. Hence Λ̃ is linear on the space of compactly supported continuous fields with support in U, extends Λ (take hᵢ = g for g ∈ C¹), and |Λ̃(g)| ≤ c(W) sup|g| whenever spt g is a compact subset of the open W ⊂⊂ U. In particular Λ̃ is a locally bounded linear functional on C_c(U, ℝ^N) (U with the subspace topology is locally compact Hausdorff; continuous fields with compact support in U correspond to elements of C_c(U, ℝ^N) by restriction and extension by 0).

5. “⇒”, Step 3: Riesz representation (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14, chapter-01.txt line 1654; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_14 for the locally compact Hausdorff space X := U and H := ℝ^N). There are a Radon measure μ_U on U and a μ_U-measurable ν_U : U → ℝ^N with |ν_U| = 1 μ_U-a.e. and Λ̃(g) = ∫_U ⟨g, ν_U⟩ dμ_U for all g ∈ C_c(U, ℝ^N). Let μ be the Borel measure on ℝ^N given by μ(B) := μ_U(B ∩ U) (push-forward under the inclusion; Borel sets of U are traces of Borel sets of ℝ^N because U is open), and ν := −ν_U on U, ν := e₁ off U. Here simon_theorem_4_14 provides a Radon outer measure with ν_U measurable for its Carathéodory σ-algebra; since μ_U is Borel regular on the σ-compact space U, every μ_U-measurable set differs from a Borel set by a μ_U-null set, so ν_U = ν̃_U μ_U-a.e. for a Borel ν̃_U, and integrals of Borel integrands against the Carathéodory measure equal those against its restriction to Borel sets; use ν̃_U in place of ν_U. Then μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) = μ_U(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (Radon), ν is Borel, hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable, with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e., and for C¹ g with compact support in U: ∫_{E∩U} div g = Λ(g) = Λ̃(g) = ∫⟨g, ν_U⟩dμ = −∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ. So (μ, ν) is a Gauss-Green pair.

6. Uniqueness, Step 1. Let (μ, ν), (μ', ν') be pairs. By (GG), ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ = ∫⟨g, ν'⟩dμ' for all C¹ g with compact support in U; by mollification (uniform convergence with supports in a fixed compact subset of U, where μ, μ' are finite, and dominated convergence) the identity extends to all continuous g with compact support in U.

7. Uniqueness, Step 2: total variation on open sets (Simon Ch. 2, (2.4), lines 518-526: |Du| “is uniquely characterized by” its values on open W ⊂⊂ U). For open O ⊆ U: μ(O) = sup{∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ : g continuous, spt g compact ⊆ O, |g| ≤ 1}. “≥” follows from (R2)-type estimate ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≤ ∫_O |g| dμ ≤ μ(O). “≤”: let K ⊆ O be compact and ε > 0. Choose a compact L ⊆ O with K ⊆ int L and μ(L ∖ K) < ε (the closed η-neighbourhoods L_η of K decrease to K, μ(L_η) < ∞ for small η). By Lusin's theorem (SimonGMT IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.simon_theorem_1_17 or Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable for the finite measure μ⌞L, applied to the N real coordinates of ν with error ε/(2N) each, and intersecting the resulting closed sets; also discard the null set where |ν| ≠ 1) there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K') < ε on which ν is continuous with |ν| = 1. Extend ν|K' to a continuous map ℝ^N → ℝ^N (Tietze, coordinatewise), compose with the radial retraction r(z) := z/max(1, |z|) onto the closed unit ball, and multiply by a continuous cut-off χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K, spt χ ⊆ L. The resulting g is admissible and ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≥ μ(K') − μ(L ∖ K') ≥ μ(K) − ε − (μ(L ∖ K) + ε) ≥ μ(K) − 3ε. Since μ(O) = sup{μ(K) : K ⊆ O compact} (inner regularity of the locally finite Borel measure μ⌞U on the open set U), “≤” follows. The same holds for (μ', ν'), and by Step 6 the two suprema coincide: μ(O) = μ'(O) for every open O ⊆ U.

8. Uniqueness, Step 3: μ = μ'. Both measures vanish on ℝ^N ∖ U and are locally finite Borel measures on the σ-compact open set U, hence outer regular there; agreeing on open subsets of U, they agree on all Borel subsets of U, and μ(B) = μ(B ∩ U) = μ'(B ∩ U) = μ'(B) for every Borel B. So μ = μ'.

9. Uniqueness, Step 4: ν = ν' μ-a.e. With μ = μ', ∫⟨g, ν − ν'⟩dμ = 0 for all continuous g with compact support in U (Step 6). Fix a compact K ⊆ U. Continuous compactly supported fields are dense in L¹(μ⌞L; ℝ^N) for a compact neighbourhood L ⊆ U of K; choose such gᵢ → (ν − ν')1_K in L¹(μ) with |gᵢ| ≤ 2 (truncate by the radial retraction onto the ball of radius 2). Since ν − ν' is bounded, ∫_K |ν − ν'|² dμ = lim ∫⟨gᵢ, ν − ν'⟩dμ = 0, so ν = ν' μ-a.e. on K. U is a countable union of compact sets and μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, so ν = ν' μ-a.e. ∎
key_steps: '⇐': the pair identity bounds ∫_W χ_E div g by μ(W̄)·sup|g|.
'⇒': the BV bound makes g ↦ ∫_{E∩U} div g locally bounded on C¹ fields; extend by mollification to compactly supported continuous fields.
Riesz representation (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14; SimonGMT simon_theorem_4_14) on U gives μ_U, ν_U; push μ_U to ℝ^{n+1} and set ν := −ν_U (Borel version).
Uniqueness: the pairings ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ agree for all continuous compactly supported g.
μ(O) = sup{∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ : |g| ≤ 1, spt g ⊆ O} (Lusin + Tietze), so μ and μ' agree on open subsets of U, hence everywhere (outer regularity).
ν = ν' μ-a.e. by density of continuous fields in L¹(μ⌞K).
